deities: Lord Shiva as Grishneshwar Jyotirlinga (12th Jyotirlinga; 'lord of compassion')
Goddess Parvati (traditional consort, worshipped in the complex)
festivals: Maha Shivaratri (most important festival; very large crowds, extended darshan)
Shravan month (July-August; extended timings approx. 3:00 AM-11:00 PM)

history.dynasty: Maratha reconstruction by Maloji Bhosale (16th century) and Queen Ahilyabai Holkar of Indore (18th century); original temple traditionally 13th century
history.summary: Grishneshwar at Verul, near the Ellora Caves about 30 km from Aurangabad, is the 12th and last of the Jyotirlingas of Shiva, with the name 'Grishneshwar' meaning 'lord of compassion'. The original temple is traditionally dated to the 13th century and was destroyed during the Delhi Sultanate incursions of the 13th-14th centuries. It went through repeated cycles of rebuilding and re-destruction during the Mughal-Maratha conflicts. The temple was reconstructed by Maloji Bhosale of Verul, the grandfather of Chhatrapati Shivaji, in the 16th century, and was rebuilt in its present form in the 18th century under the sponsorship of Maharani Ahilyabai Holkar of Indore after the decline of Mughal power. The central legend holds that the devout woman Ghushma, whose son was murdered, continued her Shiva worship with unshaken faith; pleased by her devotion, Shiva manifested here as a Jyotirlinga and, at her request, remained at the site for the welfare of devotees. Built in red volcanic stone with a five-tier shikhara, the temple shows Maratha-style architecture with intricate carvings of gods, goddesses and mythological scenes, including the Dashavatara carvings on the walls. It remains an active pilgrimage site where completing the twelve-Jyotirlinga yatra is seen as the fulfilment of a lifetime vow.

name: Grishneshwar Temple
town_description: Aurangabad, now officially Chhatrapati Sambhajinagar, is the historic capital of the Marathwada region in Maharashtra and the gateway to the UNESCO World Heritage sites of the Ajanta and Ellora Caves. It grew around the 17th-century city founded by the Mughals as Aurangabad and later became a major Maratha and Nizam-era centre, with monuments such as the Bibi ka Maqbara and the Daulatabad Fort. Grishneshwar Temple lies about 30 km northwest at Verul, next to the Ellora Caves.

travel.airport: Chhatrapati Sambhajinagar (Aurangabad) Airport (approx. 30 km; taxis and app cabs available).
travel.railway: Aurangabad Railway Station (approx. 30 km), well connected to Mumbai, Pune and other cities; autos and taxis to Verul.
travel.road: About 30 km northwest of Aurangabad on the Aurangabad-Ellora road; regular MSRTC and private buses, autos and taxis run from Aurangabad to Ellora/Verul. Ellora Caves are about 1 km from the temple; Ajanta Caves about 100 km.

visitor_information.best_time: October to March for pleasant weather. Maha Shivaratri and Shravan month are the most significant times but very crowded; weekday early mornings are best for peaceful darshan.
visitor_information.opening_hours: Approx. 5:30 AM to 9:30 PM daily (verify - some sources list 5:00 AM opening; Shravan month extended timings approx. 3:00 AM-11:00 PM). Free entry. Traditional dress advised. Men must go bare-chested to enter the garbhagriha sanctum; leather items, cameras and mobile phones are restricted inside.
